description: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of inference compute steps (x-axis) and majority voting accuracy (y-axis) for two distinct models, as presented in the paper “Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners.” The x-axis, labeled “Number of,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with major tick marks at each power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Majority voting accuracy,” is linear and spans from 0.3 to 0.6, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Two lines are plotted: the upper line, marked with green triangles and a solid blue line, begins at approximately 0.43 at 2⁰, rises sharply to 0.50 at 2², continues increasing gradually to 0.57 at 2⁶, and plateaus near 0.60 from 2⁷ to 2⁸. The lower line, marked with light blue circles and a dashed light blue line, starts near 0.25 at 2⁰, climbs steadily to 0.40 at 2⁴, reaches 0.43 at 2⁶, and stabilizes around 0.44 from 2⁷ to 2⁸. Both lines exhibit diminishing returns in accuracy gains as the number of compute steps increases.
